title: analytics: a dimension through a lookup answers 500 DATABASE_ERROR past the dialect bind limit (FK-expand id list) — compile it to a JOIN … GROUP BY on SQL drivers
body:
domain:server#5 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cztR1A2CZoxSZyuoGP

Filing gate: ① a reproduced product defect with a named seam. Child of epic #33631 (SQL performance), item R2 of the M0 ranked list (#33633, comment https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/33631#issuecomment-6889544281).

## What happens

`POST /analytics/query` with a dimension through a lookup answers **500 `DATABASE_ERROR`** once the base set holds more distinct FK values than the dialect's bind limit.

- reach: public door, measured once on both dialects by the M0 bench (`packages/qa/dogfood/bench/sql-perf`, PR #33662): cube `bench_line_item`, `dimensions: ['opportunity.stage']`, 100k distinct opportunities.
  - SQLite: `too many SQL variables`.
  - PostgreSQL: `bind message has 34464 parameter formats but 0 parameters` (100,000 mod 65,536).
- Seam: `service-analytics` `ObjectQLStrategy#resolveFkAttr` (`objectql-strategy.ts` ~1765) builds `id IN (every distinct FK value)`, then `rebucketCrossObject` (~1723) re-buckets in the app.

## Expected (epic #33631 rules)

On SQL drivers, one `JOIN … GROUP BY parent.attr` in the database: no id list, no bind-count ceiling. M0 measured PG 182 ms → 131 ms for the first read alone, and the read stops failing. Each hop keeps the related object's read scope and tenant wall, with a parity test against the current path. Non-SQL drivers follow the #33626 rulings (memory keeps in-process; MongoDB/OData refuse with a stable 400).

## Business reason

A dashboard grouped by a lookup's field (opportunity stage, account industry) over a large detail table fails outright instead of answering. Analytics over real data volumes is the case the epic exists for.

## Reader

domain:server#5 area A3 (service-analytics), next account; size M. Before/after on the M0 baseline in the PR.

## Dedupe

`repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack is:issue resolveFkAttr` → 14 hits (open: only #33631, #33633); `"too many SQL variables"` → 9 hits (open: only #33631, #33633); `analytics dimension lookup bind limit` → 35 hits, none on this seam.
